Sydney housing market under severe stress with auction reality check; REITs and banks face credit headwinds (#52, #65, #46)

Super contributions surge >33% post-budget tax changes; new government-backed digital pension scheme proposed (#62, #67)
Global macro risks: China political instability (Xi ally expelled), Trump trade war straining global supply chains (#28, #6, #47)
Fuel price shock rising; EV adoption accelerating as consumers flee petrol (#54, #68)
US markets resilient: Dow +450pts, Nvidia extends gains, AI optimism persists despite antitrust suit (#7, #4, #5)

sectors.trend: Iron ore downside pressure weighs on major miners; gold exploration sector active with multiple WA/SA discoveries; rare earths (Dalaroo/Greenland) and antimony-gold (Larvotto) diversify pipeline
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face margin compression on iron ore; gold juniors (PLA.AX, BHP-related SA plays, DLR.AX, LRV.AX, FRA.AX, GSO.AX) attract speculative flows; rare earths offer strategic premium

sectors.trend: Housing market bloodbath in Sydney and auction reality check raise NPL concerns; higher-rate environment pressures mortgage demand; super contribution surge supports fund managers
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face credit cycle risk in property; super fund managers (HUB.AX, PPA.AX) benefit from 33%+ contribution surge; digital pension scheme (#67) could disrupt traditional super model long-term

sectors.trend: Diesel/petrol price shock rising; EV adoption accelerating; bulk carrier grounding at Gladstone flags shipping/logistics disruption
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, WLE.AX face fuel cost inflation; EV transition benefits battery/charging infrastructure names; Gladstone incident (#26) may disrupt coal/LNG export logistics short-term

sectors.trend: US AI optimism (BofA survey, Nvidia gains) but antitrust suit and AI bottleneck concerns; tokenised equities threaten incumbents like Broadridge
sectors.implications: ASX tech names (WTC.AX, XRO.AX) benefit from global AI capex cycle; disruption risk to financial infrastructure providers; Ciena 58% upside thesis signals network infrastructure demand

sectors.trend: Housing affordability crisis deepens; rental market reform proposed (cutting out agents); immigration debate intensifies
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICOL.AX, DGL.AX) face occupancy/rental yield pressure; WES.AX, WOW.AX pressured by consumer cost-of-living squeeze; immigration policy uncertainty affects labour supply

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely range-bound to modestly lower over 1-3 months. RBA hawkishness (Bullock) and iron ore weakness cap upside; housing stress and fuel inflation weigh on consumer and property sectors. Gold miners and super managers provide relative outperformance. Dow resilience and AI optimism offer some global support but antitrust risks loom.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautiously constructive if RBA pauses and iron ore stabilises. Structural themes: super contribution growth, critical minerals/gold exploration pipeline, EV transition, and AI infrastructure buildout support selective equity returns. Key risk: prolonged rate cycle or China demand collapse could extend correction.
